rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 13's paragraph runs: concrete list ('A fact. A role. A preference. A constraint.') -> generalisation 1 ('All of it colors what comes next.') -> generalisation 2 ('You, in a way, compel the right output by having the right stuff in the context.') -- two generalising sentences stacked on one concrete list where the rule licenses one. Deletion test: cutting either sentence and reading straight into line 15's closer ('The move is loading the right context before the question...') still reads clean, which is the tell that one of the two is the restatement. Two-sided read acknowledged: sentence 1 states the mechanism, sentence 2 reframes it as reader agency, so a genuine second job is arguable -- filing as non-blocking per the rule's own 'not a REVISE on its own' caveat.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut 'All of it colors what comes next.' and let the list run straight into the agency sentence, or fold the two into one ('you compel the right output by having the right stuff in the context').
